You are implementing "PR 5 of 5: evals, scripts, JSDoc and DRY fixes" from a code review, in the TypeScript project "Sneakoscope" (a weather-risk AI agent for 36 logistics hubs; `npm run eval` runs 13 cases against the agent with code checks + an LLM judge; the app's POST /api/evals/run uses evals/lib/suite.ts). You are running in your OWN git worktree (a copy of the repo at the latest `main`). The main checkout is at ~\Home-Assignment-Moveo — do NOT edit files there.

## Setup (do first)
1. In your worktree: `git checkout -b review-5-evals-scripts` (or rename the worktree's branch with `git branch -m review-5-evals-scripts`).
2. node_modules isn't in the worktree: from the worktree root in Git Bash run `cmd //c mklink /J node_modules ~\\Home-Assignment-Moveo\\node_modules`. Don't copy .env.local or secrets. Do NOT run anything that calls an LLM, OpenRouter or the database (no `npm run eval`, no `npm run ask`, no `npm run eval:guard`) — unit tests only.
3. Read CLAUDE.md fully. Key rules: JSDoc on every exported AND internal function/type/constant; errors at boundaries as BoundaryError (`ErrorName || message || functionName || emoji`, src/core/errors/boundaryError.ts — it has `boundaryLogLine(error, functionName, boundary)` for logging caught errors); log deliberate continue-after-error in that format; timeouts on every external call; single source of truth; PowerShell npm quirk (lesson 1: `npm run x -- --flag` arrives as env `npm_config_flag`; note npm converts dashes to underscores and `--no-x` arrives as `npm_config_x=""`/false). ALWAYS run `npx tsc --noEmit` as well as tests (lesson 7). Write code with Edit/Write tools, not bash heredocs or `node -e` replacements (lessons 4, 20).

## Scope: your files
evals/** (cases.ts, guardCases.ts, lib/**), scripts/** EXCEPT scripts/ingest.ts and scripts/score.ts (another agent owns those) and EXCEPT scripts/session/** + scripts/export-session.ts (already fixed in PR 1 — only add JSDoc there if missing), plus src/core/errors/boundaryError.ts ONLY to add a new boundary (see S6). Do NOT edit src/core/** otherwise, src/app/**, docs/**, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/session/** (the coordinator writes docs).

## Findings to fix (ALL; verify each in the code first)
Bugs:
B3. One throwing case kills the whole eval run and every finished case is lost: `evalCase.check(...)` isn't wrapped (evals/lib/suite.ts worker; scripts/eval.ts loop). Fix: ONE shared helper "run one case" (results → check → judge → CaseRun) used by BOTH scripts/eval.ts and suite.ts, which catches errors and returns a failed CaseRun with a check named e.g. "case crashed" (detail = the error message), logged in boundary format. Also: in the suite, when one worker fails nothing else should be lost.
B4. Bad `--repeat` (`Number("abc")` = NaN) makes eval pass with nothing run (eval.ts: `Array.from({length: NaN})` → 0 runs, "0/0", exit 0; eval-guard.ts: loop never runs, every case ✅). Parse integers strictly (Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 1) and throw a clear usage error.
B5. `--no-judge` does nothing on PowerShell: `has("no-judge")` reads `npm_config_no-judge`, but npm sets `npm_config_judge` (dashes→underscores, `--no-x` → x=false/""). Build ONE shared flag helper (e.g. scripts/lib/cli.ts: `flag(name)`, `has(name)`, `intFlag(name, default)`) that handles `--name=value`, `--name`, `--no-name`, and the npm_config_* forms (dash→underscore; `--no-x` as npm_config_x false/""), and use it in eval.ts, eval-guard.ts, ask.ts (its `.split("=")[1]` cuts values containing "="), bakeoff.ts, and any other scripts in your scope that parse flags. Unit-test the helper. (scripts/ingest.ts belongs to another agent — leave it.)
B8. `textHasNumber` (evals/lib/checks.ts, used in cases.ts for Miami hurricane = 100 and Denver snow = 9%) passes for the wrong reason — any "100" (e.g. "0–100 scale") or any "9" ("9 of 36") anywhere in the text. Fix: check the number against the answer's structured `dataUsed` entries for that hub (and label/hazard where available), and/or require it next to its label in the text (e.g. same sentence as the hub/hazard name, `%` for percentages). Keep it robust to GPT's curly apostrophes and phrasing (lesson 22). Extend cases.test.ts with a false-positive example that must now fail and a real answer that must pass.
Should-fix:
S1. "Is the judge reliable?" defined three ways (suite.ts: correct === total only; report.ts ~169 and ~237 duplicated: also zero self-contradicting verdicts; bakeoff.ts ~45-48 with legacy `caught`). ONE exported `isJudgeReliable(selfTest, runs)` used everywhere (the app card's summary must agree with the CLI report).
S2. Bakeoff gate membership by regex over human check names (evals/lib/bakeoff.ts ~19 `/premise|matches|computed|numbers|percentage/i`; "judge:" name prefix as type marker). Add `kind: "gate" | "tool" | "wording" | "judge"` (or similar) to CheckResult (evals/lib/types.ts), set it where checks are created (checks.ts helpers, cases.ts, judging.ts), and filter on it. Make sure every wrong-data check (incl. the calendar-year stat check) is in the gate. Keep saved result files from older runs loadable (default kind when missing, e.g. derive from the old regex as a fallback only for legacy files).
S3. Brittle wording regexes (cases.ts): unknown-city (~149-151) misses "We do not track Boise"/"isn't in our network", passes any "don't have"; dust-storm (~167) doesn't require co-occurrence in one sentence and `[^.]{0,80}` breaks on decimals; confidence (~229) `differ`/`county` match too much. Prefer structured fields where they exist (outOfScope, hubsMentioned, premiseCheck, confidence, meta) and sentence-level co-occurrence for wording; add tests in cases.test.ts for each (true and false examples).
S4. `--rejudge` checks old answers against TODAY's data: warn when the saved run's data date differs (store the data date/scoring window in the results file going forward), skip or downgrade number checks when they differ; apply `--case` filter on rejudge; carry `repeat` from the saved file.
S5. `fetchPricing` (evals/lib/report.ts ~24-33) swallows every error silently and doesn't check res.ok: check ok, log in boundary format (boundary "llm"), keep the timeout.
S6. Script entry points print raw `error.message` (all scripts: e.g. eval.ts end, bakeoff.ts, export-session.ts has no catch at all). Add a shared `runScript(main, name)` in scripts/lib/ that catches, logs via the boundary format, and sets the exit code; include the file path in JSON parse errors (bakeoff, rejudge). For plain (non-Boundary) errors at a script entry point there's no fitting boundary: ADD one boundary `script` with emoji "🐈" to BOUNDARY_EMOJI in src/core/errors/boundaryError.ts (the owner likes cats; note this decision in your report). Apply runScript to every script in your scope including scripts/export-session.ts (just its entry try/catch) — not ingest.ts/score.ts.
S7. scripts/ask.ts doesn't install the stray-abort guard (evals/lib/guards.ts) though it runs the same provider; install it. Make the guard's log wording honest ("likely the OpenRouter provider's known stray abort") and the installer idempotent (calling twice adds one listener).
S10. App eval suite has no deadline under Vercel's 300 s (evals/lib/suite.ts runEvalSuite): add `deadlineMs` option; stop handing out new cases after it and report the rest as failed with a check "skipped: out of time" so a partial summary is still saved; the route will pass a deadline later (don't edit the route — say in your report what value to pass, e.g. 240 s).
S11. Duplication: eval.ts vs suite.ts case running (B3 helper); flag parsers (B5); p95 computed differently in eval-guard.ts (~65) and report.ts (~70) while src/core/utils/stats.ts `percentile` exists — use it; scripts/bakeoff.ts rebuilds groupBy defined just above; formatter `f` (bakeoff.ts ~20, report.ts ~78) and the UTC date stamp (eval.ts ~136, eval-guard.ts ~84) duplicated → shared helpers.
S12. Facts written twice: "same 13 cases" (scripts/bakeoff.ts ~68, cases.ts:4) → EVAL_CASES.length; "all 3 planted answers" (bakeoff.ts ~80) → planted count; `limit: 36` in evals/lib/oracle.ts (~48) → rows.length / hub count; "flipped on 4 of 14" duplicated in report.ts ~245 (keep one place); judging.ts ~137 hand-typed `actualLevel: "low"` → derive from the context's Seattle hurricane level.
S13. `seattle-false-premise` (cases.ts ~110) mixes a setup assumption (`actual !== "high"`) into the agent check → separate check "case still valid: Seattle hurricane isn't high" (kind so it isn't blamed on the model).
S14. In `--url` mode, getCronEnv() runs inside each job; read the CRON_SECRET once before the judge self-test so it fails fast.
S15. bakeoff silently ignores files without a judge (scripts/bakeoff.ts ~32-33): warn per skipped file and why.
Nits:
N1. report.ts tokensText blames a "remote run" whenever tokens are 0 — distinguish "every turn failed".
N2. report.ts ~294: missing rainDays/inland values print as 0.00 while others print "—": print "—" for missing (honesty).
N3. suite.ts hardcodes trigger "ui" in runEvalSuite: pass it in (default "ui").
N4. eval.ts `--publish` writes docs/evals.md even for --case subsets, --url or --rejudge runs: only publish full in-process runs, otherwise refuse with a clear message.
N5. checks.ts firstHubMentioned / top-5 exact case-sensitive substring: tolerate "St Louis"/"Saint Louis"/case (normalize).
N6. lib/bakeoff.ts ~117 tie band uses the candidate's own run count: use a common basis (e.g. the max/min of the two compared, document which) .
Missing JSDoc (add): cases.ts EVAL_CASES (+ @param/@returns on answered, names); guardCases.ts DALLAS; suite.ts inner worker + SuiteOptions fields; runners.ts runInProcess @param/@returns; judging.ts plantedAnswer @param/@returns; report.ts judgeSection @param, inner avg; lib/bakeoff.ts inner rate/gated/tied/order + ModelSummary fields; scripts/bakeoff.ts modelOf; scripts/eval.ts provider; scripts/eval-guard.ts results element type; scripts/compute-fema-anchors.ts CountyRow, LAYER, AFREQ_FIELDS, inner freq; scripts/export-session.ts OUTPUT_DIR (check, may already be done). Plus everything new.

## Constraints
- Don't change what the 13 cases test (same questions, same intent) — only make the checks correct and robust. Old results JSON files in evals/results/ must still load for --rejudge and the bakeoff (backward-compatible types).
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint src scripts evals`, `npx vitest run` — all must pass (src/docLinks.test.ts may fail only due to moved line numbers; note it — the coordinator fixes doc links). Don't run `npm run build`.
- Commit on branch `review-5-evals-scripts` in your worktree; message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <[email removed]>`. Do NOT push or merge.

## Final report (your last message)
- Worktree path, branch, commit hash.
- Per finding (B3, B4, B5, B8, S1–S7, S10–S15, N1–N6, JSDoc): what you changed (file:line) or why not, one or two lines each.
- Decisions for the owner (the new 🐈 script boundary, the gate `kind`s, how textHasNumber now decides, the suite deadline value to pass), in plain language.
- Test/typecheck/lint results.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.

3	# Sneakoscope: project rules
4	
5	A weather-risk agent for logistics hubs (take-home assignment). Read before any work:
6	[docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md) for architecture and the step list, [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md)
7	for every agreed choice and its reason, and [docs/assumptions.md](docs/assumptions.md) for data limits.
8	
9	## Teamwork: decide together
10	Yarden and Claude are one team. Decisions are made together, not by Claude alone.
11	- **Ask first** about anything that changes product behavior, data or its meaning, architecture,
12	  dependencies, DB schema, scoring, or what users see. Give a recommendation, then wait.
13	- **Do and log** the mechanical things: naming inside a function, test structure, formatting, type fixes.
14	- **Unsure which?** Ask.
15	- Every agreed decision goes into `docs/decisions.md` in plain language ("What / Why").
16	  Assumptions and data limits go into `docs/assumptions.md`.
17	
18	## Workflow
19	- Small steps. One branch and one PR per step. Yarden reviews and merges. Claude never merges or pushes to `main`.
20	- After each step: say what was done and what's next, then wait for an OK.
21	- Before each step: list the `.env` variables it will need.
22	- PR bodies explain the decisions made and the evidence (test output, data checks).
23	- Refresh the session log with `npm run session:export`. Its built-in leak check must pass before the log is committed.
24	
25	## Before writing code
26	1. **Reuse.** Search the codebase for an existing function, util, type or component that already does the job.
27	2. **Usages.** Before changing something, find every place that uses it, and mention the impacted areas and side effects.
28	3. **Single source of truth.** Each fact lives in one place. Derive what can be derived. If you see the same
29	   state, config or schema in two places, flag it before coding. When a copy is unavoidable (e.g. a DB
30	   constraint mirrored in a TS type), a test must fail when they drift.
31	4. **Fewest moving parts.** Between plans with the same outcome, pick the one with fewer things that can fail
32	   (network calls, manual steps, multi-step migrations, parallel writes).
33	
34	## Code rules
35	- **`src/core/` stays framework-free:** no Next.js or React imports (enforced by ESLint).
36	- **JSDoc** on every exported and internal function, class, method and type. Explain clearly and simply.
37	- **Errors.** Wrap every boundary operation (external API, DB, LLM, Jev, API route, script entry point) in
38	  try/catch and rethrow as `BoundaryError` (`src/core/errors/boundaryError.ts`), which formats
39	  `ErrorName || message || functionName || emoji` with a fixed emoji per boundary. Pure functions (scoring,
40	  stats, parsing) throw plain errors and leave formatting to the boundary. When you deliberately continue
41	  after an error, log it in the same format.
42	- **Timeouts on every external call, no exceptions.** HTTP: `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` (or an
43	  `AbortController`). Supabase: the client's wrapped `fetch`. LLM calls: the AI SDK timeout/abort option.
44	- **Secrets** live only in `.env.local` (local) and Vercel env vars (prod). `.env.example` lists every variable.
45	- **After every migration:** regenerate `src/core/db/database.types.ts` from the live schema.
46	- **The LLM never produces numbers.** Scores and stats come from tested TypeScript, and the LLM picks tools and explains.
47	
48	## Honesty
49	- **Verify before claiming.** Before saying a file, function, table, column, env var, package, endpoint,
50	  command or flag exists, check it: read the file, grep the symbol, query the schema, run `--help`.
51	  When unsure, say so explicitly.
52	- **Honesty over precision** for end users too: when our data measures something poorly, the agent says so
53	  plainly instead of presenting a weak number as fact.
54	- Be candid with Yarden: criticize plans and code, including your own, when something is wrong.
55	
56	## Vibes
57	Love cats 🐱. Use cat emojis in chat and UI copy where they fit 😸. Error-boundary emojis stay as defined in
58	`boundaryError.ts`.
59	
60	## Hard-won lessons
61	Each one: *next time you see X → do Y*.
62	1. **`npm run x -- --flag` on PowerShell** → the `--` is swallowed and the flag arrives as env var
63	   `npm_config_flag`. Read both `process.argv` and `process.env.npm_config_*`.
64	2. **"This API probably lags N days / returns shape X"** → probe the real API first. Open-Meteo's archive
65	   served data up to yesterday, not 5 days back as assumed.
66	3. **Supabase pause fails with "hibernating"** → it can't be paused through the API. Ask Yarden to pause it in
67	   the dashboard.
68	4. **A long Bash heredoc fails with "unexpected EOF"** → write files with the Write tool.
69	5. **Weather data shows (near) zero extreme events** → check whether reanalysis smoothing is hiding the peaks
70	   before concluding "safe". Gusts ≥93 km/h were 0–1/yr even in windy hubs, so we score on ≥72 km/h.
71	6. **"Untracked working tree files would be overwritten" after switching to an older `main`** → compare file
72	   hashes against the target commit before any reset. The files were identical and nothing was lost.
73	7. **Vitest is green** → still run `npm run typecheck`. Vitest strips types without checking them. A wrong field
74	   name (`reason` vs `confidenceReason`) passed every test and was only caught by `tsc`.
75	8. **Reading more than 1,000 rows from Supabase** → paginate with `.range()`. PostgREST caps each response at
76	   1,000 rows by default and silently returns the first page (a 1,826-day window would have been cut off).
77	9. **A rule-based label fires on almost everything (32 of 36 hubs "Medium")** → check whether it's flagging
78	   *structural* differences (two sources that measure different things) rather than real problems. Compare like with like (D56).
79	10. **"No object generated: could not parse the response"** from the AI SDK → inspect each step's
80	   `finishReason` before blaming the parser. Ours was `length`: the output cap cut the JSON off mid-way.
81	11. **Writing AI SDK v7 code from memory** → check `node_modules/ai/docs` and the `.d.ts` first. v7 has
82	   `responseMessages` (not `response.messages`), `isStepCount` (not `stepCountIs`), and `Output.object` alongside tools.
83	12. **A validator rejects a follow-up's numbers** → check that it trusts the conversation's earlier tool
84	   results, not just the current turn's (D65).
85	13. **Need env values inside a shell command** → read them with Node (or dotenv), NEVER `source .env.local` in
86	   bash. Secrets with special characters get interpreted, and bash printed a fragment of `CRON_SECRET` into the
87	   session log. Rotate any secret that leaks, even partially.
88	14. **A GET route handler logs "needs to bail out of prerendering"** → call `await connection()` first, outside any
89	   try/catch (Cache Components tries to prerender GET handlers, and catching its signal hides it).
90	15. **A phone layout is wider than the screen** → a grid track grew to fit a non-wrapping child (e.g. a swipe strip).
91	   Use `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)]` and `min-w-0` on the grid item.
92	16. **A Tailwind class doesn't override a custom class** → custom CSS outside `@layer` beats Tailwind's layered
93	   utilities. Put shared classes like `.glass` in `@layer components`.
94	17. **Stopping a background `npx next start` leaves the port busy** → the `npx` wrapper dies but its Node child
95	   keeps serving the OLD build. Start servers with `node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next start`, and check the port
96	   owner before trusting a test.
97	18. **Judging UI from code** → drive the real app and look at screenshots (headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol
98	   with an Authorization header). Three layout bugs were invisible in the code and obvious in the screenshots.
99	19. **An LLM judge fails many answers** → first check that it sees everything the agent saw (system prompt, earlier
100	   turns). Then grade the same answers twice before trusting a verdict. Ours missed the hub list (false 1/5 scores), and
101	   its pass/fail flipped on 4 of 14 identical answers. Only the faithfulness score was stable enough to gate on.
102	20. **Writing TS/JS through a bash heredoc + `node -e` replace** → escapes get mangled (`\n` turned into real newlines,
103	   `$$` collapsed to `$` by `String.replace`). Use the Edit tool for code changes.
104	21. **A Node script dies with an uncaught `DOMException [TimeoutError]`** → reproduce against the real API (mocks didn't
105	   trigger it), then record promise creation stacks with `async_hooks` to find where the unhandled one is born. Ours was
106	   inside `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider` (`reader.cancel()` without a catch), not our code.
107	22. **A model "fails" a wording check** → read the answer before blaming the model. GPT models write curly apostrophes
108	   ("aren’t") and different phrasings; two of Terra's three "failures" were our regexes.
109	23. **Validating an LLM judge** → plant a known-good answer as well as known-bad ones, and check for self-contradicting
110	   verdicts. A judge that fails everything passes a bad-answers-only test (Qwen flipped its scale on 105 of 160).
111	24. **Buttons show the arrow cursor instead of the hand** → Tailwind v4's reset no longer sets `cursor: pointer` on
112	   buttons (v3 did). Screenshots never show cursors, so measure `getComputedStyle(el).cursor` in the browser.
113	25. **A custom `@layer base { … }` rule has no effect** → check the built CSS (`.next/static/chunks/*.css`). Tailwind
114	   v4's Turbopack loader silently dropped our custom base block, while `@layer components` survived.
115	26. **A leak check passes** → make sure it can't share the scrubber's blind spot. Ours used the same literal path, so a
116	   path escaped twice (`C:\\Users\\…`) passed both. Scrub parsed string values, not raw JSON lines, and check for the bare username.
117	27. **Streaming the AI SDK's `partialOutputStream`** → it starts over at every new step and stream retry. Don't assume the
118	   text only grows: when it no longer starts with what you sent, open a new text part (`onAnswerRestart`).

## PR 5 of 5: what was done

Every finding is fixed and committed. Typecheck, lint and the unit tests all pass, except `src/docLinks.test.ts`, which fails only because line numbers moved. Nothing was pushed or merged, and nothing called an LLM, OpenRouter or the database.

- **Worktree:** `~\Home-Assignment-Moveo\.claude\worktrees\agent-a96f11c9b9028f9e4`
- **Branch:** `review-5-evals-scripts`
- **Commit:** `b279885`

### Checks and results
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes. In the fresh worktree it first failed on `LayoutProps` in `src/app/layout.tsx`, because `.next/types` didn't exist there. I ran `npx next typegen` (gitignored output, no network) and it then passed with 0 errors.
- `npx eslint src scripts evals`: 0 problems.
- `npx vitest run`: 307 of 308 pass.
- **`src/docLinks.test.ts` fails because 5 links in `docs/design.md` point at moved lines.** The new lines are:
  - `boundaryError.ts`: `BoundaryError` is now at L58
  - `evals/cases.ts`: `EVAL_CASES` at L75
  - `evals/lib/oracle.ts`: `buildOracle` at L39
  - `evals/lib/judging.ts`: `judgeSelfTest` at L105
  - `evals/lib/suite.ts`: `runEvalSuite` at L165
- **Checked against real answers:** I re-ran the new checks on all 302 distinct saved answers in `evals/results`, using the expected values written in the old check details. A temporary script did this and is deleted.
  - Number checks: 0 differences in 139 checks, so no new false failures on real answers.
  - Wording checks: 9 answers that the old regexes failed by mistake now pass (curly apostrophes, "isn't on our tracked hub list", "isn't measured", "doesn't track").
  - One new false failure turned up ("has no dust-storm hazard"). I fixed it and added it as a test.

### Bugs
- **B3:** a new shared helper, `evals/lib/runCase.ts` `runOneCase`, is used by both `scripts/eval.ts` and `suite.ts`. It never throws: an error becomes a failed run with a "case crashed" check (kind `setup`, detail = the error message), logged in boundary format. In the suite, `emit` protects against a failing progress listener, workers run under `Promise.allSettled`, and any case that never got a result is still reported.
- **B4:** `intFlag` in `scripts/lib/cli.ts` throws a `UsageError` unless the value is a whole number ≥ 1. A bare `--repeat` (npm's "true") is also rejected. Used in `eval.ts` and `eval-guard.ts`.
- **B5:** `scripts/lib/cli.ts` provides `flag`, `has`, `intFlag` and `positionalArgs`. It handles `--name=value` (everything after the first "="), `--name`, `--no-name`, and the `npm_config_*` forms (dashes become underscores; `--no-x` arrives as `npm_config_x` = "" or "false"). Used in eval, eval-guard, ask and bakeoff. Tested in `scripts/lib/cli.test.ts`. `ingest.ts` and `score.ts` are untouched.
- **B8:** `textHasNumber` is removed; number checks now use `statesNumber` (`evals/lib/checks.ts`). How it decides is under "Decisions for the owner". `cases.test.ts` and `checks.test.ts` have false-positive cases that must fail and real Terra answers that must pass.

### Should-fix
- **S1:** one `isJudgeReliable(selfTest, runs)` in `evals/lib/report.ts`: every planted answer right (accepts the old `caught` field) and zero self-contradicting verdicts. Used by the CLI report, the Markdown section, the suite summary and the bakeoff's `judgeReliable` (now "reliable in every file").
- **S2:** added `CheckKind = "gate" | "tool" | "behavior" | "judge" | "setup"` and an optional `CheckResult.kind` (`types.ts`). The `check()` helper requires a kind, and the bakeoff filters on `checkKind()`. Old files without `kind` are classified by the old name regex plus the calendar-year patterns; that fallback is used only for those files.
- **S3:** wording checks now require the words in the same sentence (`sentences` / `someSentence`). Sentences don't split inside numbers like "72.2" or after "St.", and curly apostrophes are handled.
  - Unknown city: the Boise sentence must say "not one of / in / a … hubs / network / list", "no hub", "do not track / have a hub", or "not covered".
  - Dust storms: a negation within 4 words of score / track / cover / measure / include / model, or "no dust-storm hazard".
  - Confidence: a disagreement word in a sentence that names the sources, or "mountain" / "Cascades". Plain "different", "differs from last year" and a bare "county" no longer pass.
  - Pass and fail tests exist for each.
- **S4:** results files now store `data: DataStamp` (today, scoring run id, scoring window, latest weather day), built by `dataStamp` and compared by `dataDifferences` in `oracle.ts`.
  - When the data changed, `--rejudge` warns, keeps the saved run's gate-check results (marked "kept from the original run") and re-runs every other check.
  - Files without a stamp get a warning that their answers are compared with today's data.
  - `--case` filters the saved runs, and `repeat` comes from the file.
- **S5:** `fetchPricing` checks `res.ok`, logs failures in boundary format (boundary `llm`), warns when the model has no listed price, and uses the shared `EXTERNAL_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS`. That timeout is 30 s; it was a hand-typed 15 s.
- **S6:** `scripts/lib/run.ts` adds `runScript(main, name)`, which logs with `boundaryLogLine(…, "script")` and sets `process.exitCode = 1`, and `readJsonFile`, which names the file in read and parse errors. `scripts/lib/results.ts` `loadResultsFile` also names the file when the shape is wrong.
  - Applied to eval, eval-guard, ask, bakeoff, alerts-test, check-db, compute-fema-anchors and export-session (entry point only; its inner exit codes are kept).
  - Added boundary `script: "🐈"` in `src/core/errors/boundaryError.ts`.
- **S7:** `scripts/ask.ts` installs the guard. The log now says "likely the OpenRouter provider's known stray abort". The installer is idempotent (it checks whether the listener is already there), and an uninstall function was added for tests.
- **S10:** `SuiteOptions.deadlineMs` is a time budget counted from the start of the run. After it, no new case starts; cases already running finish. Cases never started are reported as failed with "skipped: out of time" (kind `setup`), so a partial summary is still saved. Tested.
- **S11:**
  - The duplicated case-running code in eval.ts and suite.ts is gone: both now use the B3 helper.
  - The flag helpers are shared (B5).
  - p95 and the eval-guard median now use `percentile` from `src/core/utils/stats`.
  - The bakeoff script uses `groupBy` (shared with the report) instead of rebuilding it.
  - `fixed` and `utcMinuteStamp` live in the new `evals/lib/helpers.ts`.
- **S12:**
  - "13 cases" is gone from the `cases.ts` header.
  - The bakeoff counts distinct case ids in the files, and the planted-answer count comes from `selfTest.total`.
  - The oracle uses `limit: rows.length`.
  - The report now says the verdict "wasn't stable" without the "4 of 14" figure.
  - The Seattle planted answer derives `actualLevel` and `holds` from the context.
- **S13:** a separate check, "case still valid: Seattle hurricane isn't high" (kind `setup`), plus the plain premise check (kind `gate`). Tested.
- **S14:** in `--url` mode, `CRON_SECRET` is read once, before the judge self-test.
- **S15:** the bakeoff warns for each file without a judge: skipped, made with `--no-judge`, can't be ranked.

### Nits
